summary: Preserve the Node.js and Neo4j production mainline, TS-06 Provider E2E qualification, and canonical authority while replacing the process-only secret rule with an approved-source boundary. QWEN_KEY and ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_PASSWORD may be loaded only from direct process environment variables or the unique ignored/untracked repository-relative .argo/.env used for controlled local or protected CI execution. Process environment has precedence; differing duplicate values, unsafe file state, unapproved paths, missing or blank values, and every implicit/default fallback fail closed before provider, database, or index side effects. Zero-leakage and zero-persistence requirements remain mandatory.

Live boundary: Node runtime -> real provider -> qualification/index gate -> controlled Neo4j test instance. Network execution is explicit opt-in and restricted to controlled local or protected CI; default/offline CI fakes are required for deterministic checks but never substitute for live delivery evidence.
Failure boundary: omitted explicit model/dimensions, unapproved identity, provider error, non-finite response, or response length other than 1024 must produce zero index writes.

Approved secret-source boundary: only QWEN_KEY and ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_PASSWORD are approved secret keys. Each may originate only from a direct process environment variable or exact repository-relative .argo/.env. Process environment is higher precedence; if both sources define a key and values differ, startup fails closed. Matching duplicates may use the process value. No literal, generated, logical, nullish, ternary, command-line, alternate-file, root-.env, or other fallback source is authorized.

Secret-file boundary: .argo/.env is only for controlled local or protected CI execution and must remain ignored and untracked. Before parsing secrets, downstream design must require the canonical exact path, regular-file status, no reparse/symlink indirection, git-ignore and git-untracked evidence, no duplicate keys, and a Windows-executable ACL check that rejects broad-principal read access such as Everyone, BUILTIN\Users, or Authenticated Users while requiring the current execution identity to read. Unsafe or unverifiable state fails closed with a stable non-secret category before network, database, or index initialization.

Zero-leakage boundary: neither approved secret may enter git, stdout/stderr, error messages, logs, Cypher text or parameters, graph evidence, runner failure records, snapshots, or generated artifacts. QWEN_KEY never enters Cypher. ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_PASSWORD is consumed only by the Neo4j driver authentication connection layer and never as a query parameter. Cleanup must prove zero secret-bearing persistence and zero generated secret artifacts.

Configuration-name contract: provider profile keys remain ARGO_EMBEDDING_BASE_URL, ARGO_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS, ARGO_EMBEDDING_MODEL, ARGO_EMBEDDING_MODEL_VERSION, and ARGO_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER. Controlled Neo4j keys are ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_URL, ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_USERNAME, and ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_PASSWORD. ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_PASSWORD and QWEN_KEY follow the approved secret-source boundary; no ARGO_NEO4J_URI, ARGO_NEO4J_USERNAME, ARGO_NEO4J_PASSWORD alias or implicit fallback is authorized unless separately approved.

Example-file boundary: committed .env.example or .argo/.env.example may list approved key names with empty placeholders and non-secret instructions, but never actual secret values. Intent Design did not read, migrate, copy, or create any secret value or .argo/.env file.

Implementation Design must revise loader provenance fixtures and guards to accept direct process and exact .argo/.env sources for QWEN_KEY and ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_PASSWORD; reject alternate/tracked/root files, command-line and literal/default/fallback sources, aliases that obscure source, missing/blank values, duplicate conflicts, path traversal, reparse indirection, broad Windows ACLs, and unknown secret keys; preserve generated-canary redaction, complete value-channel scanning, and zero-persistence cleanup without reading real secret values.

Live execution prerequisites: controlled local or protected CI execution, explicit ARGO_LIVE_PROVIDER_E2E=1 opt-in, approved provider profile, exact Neo4j URL/username/password key contract, an approved secret source for both required secrets, passing source/path/ignore/tracking/ACL/conflict preflight, and a disposable controlled Neo4j instance. Default/offline checks cannot substitute for live evidence.

The new physical entrypoints tests/explicit/entries/runLiveEmbeddingProviderE2E.js and tests/explicit/entries/runLiveEmbeddingProviderSecretIsolation.js are downstream delivery targets. Their absence at Intent Design time is not acceptance evidence and does not authorize fabricated pass status.
TS-09, embedding-provider-adapter lifecycle delivery, and incremental index lifecycle remain outside this handoff; no TS-09 element, testcase, relationship, or task authorization is included.
No deliveryStatus value was changed by Intent Design; values remain runner-owned and any currently displayed status predates execution of the new physical entrypoints.
